name: Ganch Plasterwork
summary: A distinctive form of carved plasterwork unique to Central Asia, particularly Bukhara, featuring intricate geometric and floral patterns in gypsum-based material.
description: Crafted from locally sourced gypsum (ganch), this plasterwork was used to decorate interiors, domes, and portals, with artisans creating elaborate designs using specialized techniques passed down through generations. The art flourished particularly during the Timurid and Shaybanid periods as a decorative alternative to more expensive tilework.
culturalContext: Ganch — Central Asia's carved gypsum plaster — made Bukhara, Khiva and Samarkand interiors glow: ganch-dastakali deep-carved geometric and botanical reliefs (suzani-like mesh), painted-and-gilded crusts on madrasah niches, and complete room programs in muqarnas-linked panels. Masters (ustokoron) transmitted pattern families; the craft survives in restoration ateliers under UNESCO intangible-heritage programs. Ganch's whiteness turns any shaft of light into lace.
